title: Achievements poster
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 2: The Rightly Guided Caliphs: Abu Bakr and Umar
source: Written for islamic-studies/y6 lesson 21 (Pupil PDF worksheet: achievements poster)
intro: Lesson 21: Umar's rule: record-keeping, the Hijri calendar and the spread of Islam. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Organising the state
points: The diwan: a register of people and payments
New cities such as Kufa and Basra

panels.title: The Hijri calendar
points: Umar and the Companions agreed a calendar
We still use it for Ramadan and Hajj

blocks.text: One sentence in each box on how it helped people.

keywords.def: a register: a written record of people and payments
the Islamic calendar counted from the Hijrah
organising how a country is run

questions.q: Explain why the diwan helped people.
questions.a: It recorded people and payments, so support reached everyone fairly and no one was missed.

questions.q: Name one city founded in Umar's time.
Make a 'Umar's achievements' poster on the pupil PDF (four boxes: diwan, calendar, cities, Jerusalem) with one sentence each on how it helped people.
questions.a: Four accurate boxes with how each helped

questions.q: Extend: what year AH is it now? (Ask the teacher or check a calendar.)
Stretch: which of Umar's achievements matters most today? Give a reason.
questions.a: For example: the Hijri calendar, because Muslims still use it for worship

options: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ
questions.a: A) The Hijrah. Year 1 AH is the year of the Hijrah, 622 CE.

questions.q: Think again: why does a big country need records?
questions.a: To treat people fairly and make sure no one is missed.
